attributes.residual: MECHANISM NAMED, AND THE SHARED-FORM RECORD'S PRESCRIPTION IS REFUTED. Baseline real 18, insns 27/27, multiset 4t. The prior record (attempt.sndfxinitvoices-indexed-store-form-relabel.20260831.v1) predicted that the target's `add`+`stw DISP` shape 'is what base[i].member on a properly typed array yields' and that our `addi`+`stwx` 'is what raw pointer arithmetic over a byte cursor yields', so a typed-array conversion would close both functions. THAT IS NOT THE MECHANISM. Decisive counter-evidence: this function's FIRST loop and the target agree on the `add`+`stw DISP` shape from the SAME source spelling (p[345+i] etc.) that the second loop uses (p[8+i]), and sndFxInitVoices ALREADY uses fully typed struct-array indexing (st->que[i].f0, stride 20/48/36 = real struct sizes) and still emits stwx. THE ACTUAL MECHANISM is a register-role swap: the target homes the STORED VALUE in r0 (`li r0,-1` / `addi r0,r3,0`) and the address temp in a general register, so it can use `add r4,r7,r3` + `stw r0,32(r4)`; our build homes the ADDRESS TEMP in r0 (`addi r0,r3,32`), and r0 is architecturally illegal as the base register of a displacement store (it reads as literal 0), so MWCC is FORCED into `stwx r4,r6,r0`. Same four live GPRs on both sides (base, byte-IV, value, address temp) - it is a colouring permutation whose second-order effect is an addressing-mode change. AXES KILLED, all NEUTRAL at real 18 with the multiset unmoved: (1) index operand order p[8+i] -> p[i+8]; (2) explicit per-iteration element base `s32* q = &p[i]; q[8] = -1;`, which is literally the target's address shape written out. A third axis on the sibling (explicit hoisted constant locals) was also NEUTRAL. Three neutral probes across the shared form - not source-reachable by index spelling. WebFrank candidacy is real but needs its own audit class: the rewrite is a two-instruction addressing-mode substitution, not a renaming or permutation, so it carries a dataflow obligation like the live-zero family rather than fitting copy_register_fields.
